claim: A single free-recall test of studied prose beats restudy on delayed tests (2 days d=0.95, 1 week d=0.83) but loses on a 5-minute test (restudy 81% vs test 75%). The benefit appears only after a delay.
agent_test: Agent has no forgetting; test only if context is truncated or summarised between study and use: compare re-reading a note vs reconstructing it from memory after a context reset, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Three tests beat three restudy sessions at one week (61% vs 40%, d=1.26) while students predicted the opposite. Self-judged fluency is a poor guide to what sticks.
agent_test: Ask the agent to predict its own later accuracy after re-reading vs after retrieving; compare calibration at equal tokens. (Same lab and paper in all three lines, so one source.)

claim: Repeated retrieval of items beats dropping them after one correct recall; repeated restudy of recalled items adds nothing (about 80% vs 33-36% at one week, d=4.03 in one experiment; more than 100% gain in another).
agent_test: In multi-session agent memory, test whether re-quizzing notes already answered correctly once changes later accuracy vs only re-reading them. Note both papers come from one lab.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Self-regulated learners drop items after one correct recall, which is the less effective strategy. Learners choose by retrieval fluency.
agent_test: Check whether the agent stops verifying an item after one correct pass; compare fixed repeat checks with stop-after-one.

claim: Meta-analysis: testing beats restudy, g=0.50 (159 effect sizes, 81% positive, I2=84%); larger with feedback (0.73 vs 0.39) and for retention of a day or more (0.69 vs 0.41). Publication-bias caveat: g=0.50 was not bias-corrected in this note and could not be re-opened (GAP 3 open); a related re-analysis of Chan et al. 2018 (forward testing) fell from 0.44 to about 0 under bias correction.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Classroom quizzing raises achievement by g=0.499 across 222 studies and 48,478 students (confirmed in abstract this session); effect depends on control condition, feedback, repeats and format match.
agent_test: Background only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 0 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Transfer of the testing effect is weaker than direct retention: d=0.40 overall, weakest for rearranged items, untested same-study material and worked examples; publication-bias corrections often cut the intercept to no transfer without moderators.
agent_test: Test whether a self-quiz on a fact helps on a rephrased or inference question, vs re-reading the fact, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Corrective feedback matters: test plus feedback gives about 87% vs 41% test-only vs 24% no test; feedback repairs initially wrong answers (82% vs 3%) and low-confidence correct ones.
agent_test: Compare self-test with no ground truth vs self-test with a source check at equal tokens.
audit_note: Butler, Karpicke & Roediger 2008 Exp 1: .87 vs .41 vs .24; initially wrong .82 vs .03; low-confidence correct benefit shown; the figures come from one study (DOI and Rowland entries are the same PDF); Karpicke 2025 chapter agrees feedback is beneficial but moderator-dependent.

claim: Initial recall (cued or free) gives larger gains than recognition (g=0.61/0.29 vs 0.29 in the full set), consistent with effortful retrieval, but format gaps are confounded with feedback use.
agent_test: Compare agent generating an answer then checking against options vs picking from options first.

claim: Short-answer practice does not reliably beat multiple choice. Pooled d about 0.07 across four experiments (N=372), but when initial retrieval success was raised in Exp 4, short-answer and hybrid did beat MC. Retrieval success, not format, is the moderator.
agent_test: Vary difficulty of self-generated checks and measure whether success rate of 75%+ predicts benefit.

claim: Retrieval practice beats elaborative concept mapping on text learning (0.67 vs 0.45, d=1.50, N=80; replicated d about 1.0).
agent_test: Test generate-from-memory summary vs structured re-organisation of a visible document, at equal tokens. (One lab, one paper plus its own replication.)

claim: Retrieval and elaboration have separate effects. Elaboration after a first correct recall gave no measurable gain at one week in word pairs.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Elaborative-mediator accounts are weakly supported: mediator activation did not rise on retrieval trials and was unrelated or negative to cued recall; meta-analytic cue-target moderators were not significant (QB=1.83, p=.40).
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Spacing: spaced beats massed (g=0.74), expanding vs equal spacing makes little difference (g=0.03); massed retests give about 98% in-session recall but poor retention.
agent_test: Relevant only if the agent has multi-session memory with decay. Meta-analysis numbers (a14) were not opened.

claim: Retrieval attempts before study (pretesting) help for semantically related word pairs when study follows immediately (.73 vs .56 recall), but not for unrelated pairs and not when the study trial is delayed relative to the pretest (delayed pretest .55 vs .56 no pretest); this is a boundary condition on word-pair pretesting, not a statement about long retention delays.
agent_test: Have the agent attempt an answer before reading a source vs reading first; compare final accuracy at equal tokens.
audit_note: Grimaldi & Karpicke 2012: .73 vs .56 for related pairs and no effect for unrelated pairs (Exp 1) are right, but 'not after a delay' misstates Exp 3, where the delay was between the pretest and its study trial (delayed-pretest .55 vs no-pretest .56), not a retention delay; Pan and Sana 2021 shows pretesting helps in applied passage settings but does not test unrelated pairs.
claim_before_audit: Retrieval attempts before study (pretesting) help for related material when followed by study (.73 vs .56), not for unrelated pairs and not after a delay.

claim: Pretesting and posttesting both beat no test (d=1.02 and 0.76 vs control) but transfer to untested items is small (d=0.20 after pretest).
agent_test: As above.

claim: Online low-engagement samples may hide the effect: two Prolific experiments with high attrition found no significant testing effect (p=.72, p=.17). Not designed as direct replications. Counter-evidence for scope: a 2026 pre-registered N=122 study on naturalistic events found a weak-to-absent testing effect.
agent_test: Background only; engagement is a boundary condition.

claim: Practice tests reduce rather than provoke test anxiety (g=-0.52, 24 studies, N=3,374).
agent_test: Not applicable to the agent.

claim: Mixed-design comparisons (testing confounded with other factors) make up about two thirds of testing-effect comparisons and give larger effects, so the literature may overstate the clean effect. A 2025 preprint meta-analysis reports 67% mixed vs 33% direct (abstract only).
agent_test: Background only. b24 read at abstract level.

claim: Training LLMs on questions before documents (PIT) beats standard instruction tuning by 17.8 points (48.1 vs 30.3 EM, Llama-2 7B; confirmed in the arXiv paper). It is a training method, not a test of the human testing effect.
agent_test: Weights are not changed in our agent; analogy only.

claim: Self-Tuning and Allen-Zhu and Li suggest knowledge in weights is hard to extract without question-style exposure. Analogy to testing, not an LLM testing-effect study. Self-Tuning repeats the pattern on Llama2-7B, Qwen2-7B and Mistral-7B.
agent_test: Analogy only; do not use as design evidence.

claim: LLM-generated practice questions: one non-randomised class scored 0.89 vs 0.73 (n=31/27, different quiz material); in a 700-student course reviewed LLM items matched instructor items on difficulty; about two thirds of raw generated items failed review.
agent_test: For a quiz-generating agent: human or checker filtering is required.
audit_note: An et al. 2025 verified (0.89 vs 0.73, n=31/27, about 2/3 of raw MCQs unsuitable by authors' experience), but Leong et al. (700+ students, 30 LLM items) found LLM items easier (-1.01 difficulty) and less discriminating with overall weaker psychometrics, not matching instructor items; An and Wang 2026 shows LLM difficulty labels do not predict empirical difficulty.

claim: No study was found that tests a testing effect or retrieval practice inside an LLM agent at equal tokens. The agent has no forgetting, so the effect has no direct target. Absence of evidence from limited tools.
agent_test: Open question. A fair test: self-quiz after context truncation vs re-reading.

claim: AI tutoring beat in-class active learning in a crossover RCT (N=194, median post 4.5 vs 3.5, effect 0.63 by regression, 0.73 to 1.3 SD by quantile regression). Not retrieval practice specifically.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Retrieval quality, not storage, limits LLM memory systems: accuracy varied about 20 points by retrieval method vs 3 to 8 points by write strategy (LoCoMo, abstract only).
agent_test: Applies to agent memory design, not to the testing effect.

claim: Spaced-repetition models that use recall results (half-life regression) cut error by over 45% vs baselines on Duolingo logs; each review acts as a test.
agent_test: Only needed if the agent has decaying memory. Predicts recall, not delayed test performance.

claim: Publication-bias correction can shrink testing-effect meta-analytic means. Re-analysis of Chan et al. (k=159): g=0.44 fell to 0.02 (3PSM) or -0.02 (PET); standard designs 0.75 to 0.52 (3PSM). Pan and Rickard transfer intercept fell to about zero (PEESE d=0.015) while moderator effects held.
agent_test: None for the agent; use as a prior: expect smaller real effects than lab headline numbers.
audit_note: Boustani & Shanks 2022 table: overall 0.44 -> 0.02 (3PSM) / -0.02 (PET), k=159, standard 0.75 -> 0.52 (3PSM); Pan & Rickard 2018 abstract confirms intercepts substantially reduced with moderator effects minimally affected, PEESE 0.015 value only partly legible in layout. Scope slip: Chan et al. meta-analysis concerns test-potentiated new learning, not the testing effect in general.

claim: Transfer of testing depends on three stacked factors: response congruency (+0.36 PEESE), elaborated retrieval (+0.18) and initial test accuracy (+0.50 per unit). Best case predicted d=0.90 [0.71,1.08] (random effects) or 0.58 (PEESE); worst case about zero or negative.
agent_test: If the agent self-checks, log initial success rate and only trust gains above a high-success bin.

claim: Short-answer vs multiple-choice depends on feedback and initial success. Without feedback easier MC practice wins (Kang 2007: 86% vs 54% initial success); with feedback short answer wins slightly (Little 2012). LLM-assigned difficulty labels do not predict empirical difficulty (rho 0.06, n=7,888 responses).
agent_test: Measure success rate directly; do not rely on the model's own difficulty estimate.

claim: The bifurcation model says retrieved items get a large boost and unretrieved items get none while forgetting rate is equal; Karpicke argues this treats the benefit as an item-selection artifact and cites evidence for a changed forgetting rate (two lines not followed up).
agent_test: Items that fail and get no source check stay wrong; add feedback or verification on failed self-checks.

claim: No Roediger-style test-vs-restudy experiment inside an LLM context or agent loop was found. Agent papers that touch the idea use quizzes only as measurement (Task2Quiz: in-context 52.41 vs Mem0 52.36 total quiz score for one model) or learn from failures with held-out acceptance (ARISE +10.0 self, +10.9 teacher on SOP-Bench).
agent_test: A real test needs equal tokens, a leak check and a gap-detection metric.
audit_note: Task2Quiz table shows In-context 52.41 vs Mem0 52.36 total quiz score (one model row, PDF layout garbled) and ARISE +10.0 (self) / +10.9 (teacher) on SOP-Bench with held-out validation gate verified; Cao et al. contains no test-vs-restudy experiment; the negative 'none found' claim itself cannot be proven by sources.

claim: Agent self-learning gains can be artifacts: 72% of held-out migration units leaked references; leak-free memory effect fell from 0.015 to 0.002 and a copy baseline (0.222) beat all LLM systems.
agent_test: Any self-quiz test must use held-out items that do not overlap with practiced ones.

claim: Testing without any prior study can match full instruction when feedback follows (two experiments, preprint). Feedback, not retrieval from a study event, may be the active ingredient.
agent_test: Verifier or source check after an answer is the part worth copying.

claim: Field and lab effects are smaller than founding lab numbers: gateway math course (n=636/584/571) gave 4 to 5 point quiz gains and an 8 point exam gain in one cohort only; a 2025 higher-power replication found the effect independent of text complexity (N=111, N=117).
agent_test: Background only.

claim: No large pre-registered multi-site replication of Roediger and Karpicke 2006 was found. Nearest items are small pre-registered studies (N=122 naturalistic events null; N=111/117 coherence replication positive).
agent_test: Treat the founding effect as well supported but not formally replicated at scale.
